description: Empties the UpdateModelProperty inline-edit sensitive-field blocklist (compile-preserving operator: HashSet literal emptied, not deleted) and checks it against the HTTP-layer MvcAuthHolesTests that guard MVC-004's blockedFields HashSet specifically: Password and ITCode. HISTORY: as originally filed for issue #834, these tests used StudentListVM (a ListVM) and a fake Guid id, so `vm as IBaseCRUDVM<TopBasePoco>` was null and _FrameworkController.cs:540 returned the same 400 ('Entity not found') whether or not the blocklist existed -- this entry's red filter used to include the dot-notation test too and the whole set SURVIVED, which was the demonstration issue #834 asked for (see PR #839 history for that transcript). Issue #837 (PR #845, merged as f148a1383) rewrote the fixture to seed a real FrameworkUser via a real CRUD VM (FrameworkUserVM) and assert on the endpoint's own custom message text, so Password and ITCode now correctly reach the blockedFields check and this entry is KILLED. UpdateModelProperty_DotNotationField_ReturnsBadRequest was removed from this entry's red_tests: it pins a DIFFERENT, earlier, unconditional guard (`field.Contains('.')` at _FrameworkController.cs:513) that emptying blockedFields has no bearing on -- see mvc004-dotnotation-guard-neutralize below for its own mutant. It remains in this entry's green_tests instead, as a positive control proving emptying blockedFields has no effect on that sibling guard.

MVC-004: ITCode field must be blocked\. Got 200\.
